current: onboarding: read the repo, designed the account system, audited the netcode for the 20k-CCU target
notes: NEW AGENT (maintainer 2026-09-07). Owns identity, accounts, login/attach, entitlements and player-state persistence. Named account-agent, not login-agent, deliberately: the account is the thing, login is only one way to reach it.

THE ENTRY LAW I AM BOUND BY: the game is a web address you can play immediately. Today that is one tap (character preselected, name pre-filled, 'Enter world'). I MUST NOT ADD A STEP. Every player gets a silent server-side account at first join; 'create an account' is never creation, it is ATTACHING a way to log back in to the account that already holds your character. The prompt appears only once a player has something to lose.

FINDING (severity: high) — PLAYER PROGRESS IS BEING SILENTLY DELETED TODAY. games2/server/src/store.ts writes .data/players-<world>.json and .data/players-progress.json to the container filesystem. Cloud Run runs --min-instances 0 --max-instances 1, so that disk is ephemeral: it dies on every redeploy (every art push deploys) and on every idle scale-to-zero. Level, XP and inventory evaporate with no error and no log.

FINDING (severity: high) — IDENTITY IS CLIENT-INVENTED AND UNVERIFIED. net.ts getPlayerToken() mints a crypto.randomUUID() into localStorage['ml-token'] and the server believes it (WorldRoom.onJoin). Whoever knows the string IS that character: no proof of possession, no rotation, no revocation. Harmless while nothing is at stake, unrecoverable account theft the day it holds a purchase. Also iOS Safari evicts script-written storage after ~7 days.

DESIGN (maintainer-approved direction): Firestore Native in eur3 (multi-region, 99.999% SLA), server-issued HMAC-signed stateless token carrying its own expiry — the exact pattern live.ts already proved, whose comments record that an in-memory session Map signed the Game Master out on every deploy. Providers (Google, later Apple/Discord/Steam, plus passwordless email for a game-only account) are VERIFIED SERVER-SIDE and never sit in the play path; no auth aggregator holds our user table.

THE ONE RULE THAT MUST NEVER BEND: our accountId is the primary key. A provider identity is always a linked attribute, never the key. That is what keeps providers swappable, cross-platform accounts possible (web purchase visible on iOS), and Spanner reachable later if a global economy ever needs it.

NO BACKWARDS COMPATIBILITY (maintainer 2026-09-07: 'I'm the only user and I test directly in prod. So never think about backwards compatibility.'). No migration code, no schema versioning: a schema change is 'delete the collection'. TRIPWIRE: that rule holds until the first character anyone would be annoyed to lose — the maintainer's own included. Naming it in advance so the flip is a decision, not a discovery.

SCALE TARGET (maintainer 2026-09-07): 20,000 concurrent players after launch. At that load the account layer is untroubled — ~667 writes/sec on a timer, far less once writes are event-driven. Two design rules carry it: (1) separate the account of record from hot state — position changes 20x/sec and is worth nothing if lost, while level/inventory/entitlements change rarely and are worth everything, and today savePlayer writes them together on one timer; (2) write on MEANING (level-up, item gained/lost, purchase, leave), never on a fixed timer. Write amplification is the cost driver in every database and removing it is engine-independent.

requests.text:
NETCODE AUDIT FOR THE 20k-CCU TARGET — read-only, your domain, your call. The maintainer set a first goal of 20,000 concurrent players after launch and asked me to check the netcode. Measured from source, ranked, with the estimates flagged as estimates.

(1) NO INTEREST MANAGEMENT ANYWHERE — the first wall. WorldState (schema/WorldState.ts:329-334) holds players, monsters, drops, spawnAreas, chessBoards, chessMatches as plain MapSchema/ArraySchema: no @view(), no StateView, no filter. No setPatchRate either, so Colyseus's default 50ms applies — 20 full-state patches/sec to every client. the_game carries 140 monsters over 79 zones (maps2/worlds3/the_game/spawns.json), so at 200 players every client receives deltas for ~340 moving entities. ESTIMATE from entity count x typical delta size: ~140 KB/s per client, ~28 MB/s egress at 200 players, ~2.8 GB/s at 20k. The payload itself grows with population, so bandwidth is effectively O(n^2). With AOI at ~20 visible entities it is ~8 KB/s per client and stops growing with total population — roughly 17x in the_game, and the difference between impossible and routine. THE GOOD NEWS: you are already on @colyseus/core ^0.16 + @colyseus/schema ^3.0, which ship StateView/@view(). No major upgrade needed. Honest trade: per-client views make the server encode a different patch per client, so encoding goes O(entities) -> O(n x visible) — bandwidth collapses, CPU rises, which is why AOI alone still does not reach 20k on one core.

(2) SINGLE PROCESS, SINGLE CORE. Node is single-threaded and simulation plus per-client encoding share one core. No Redis presence/driver, so rooms cannot span processes; filterBy(['world']) (index.ts:203) means one room per world, so the_game's population cap IS one room's cap (maxClients = 200, WorldRoom.ts:165 — aspirational, not measured).

(3) PER-TICK O(m x (m+n)) BODY SCANS. separationPush (shared/src/monsters.ts:311) walks the whole bodies array (monsters + players) once per monster, and WorldRoom.ts:1418 does a second full scan for dodging. At 200 players: 140 x 340 x 2 ~= 95,000 distance checks per tick ~= 1.9M Math.hypot/sec on the same core. A spatial grid fixes it — monsters only care about neighbours inside a radius. Not the first wall, but it is on the same core as everything else. Credit where due: the aggro scan (WorldRoom.ts:1332) is already throttled to 450ms via m.aggroCheckAt — exactly the right instinct, it just needs applying to the other two scans.

(4) MINE, NOT YOURS — I am fixing this one. WorldRoom.ts:1776-1778 flushes every player every 30s through savePlayer, which hits JsonMapStore.save (store.ts:60-64): writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(this.data)) — the ENTIRE map of every player ever seen, serialized and fsync'd SYNCHRONOUSLY, once per player, across two stores. At 200 players that is 400 whole-file synchronous writes every 30s, each O(all accounts), ON THE GAME LOOP. The tick stops and everyone rubber-bands. The account service deletes this outright: per-account async writes, event-driven, no whole-file serialization.

SHAPE OF 20k, all estimates: ~400 players/room with AOI -> ~50 rooms -> ~50 cores -> ~13 four-core machines. Unremarkable hardware; the work is that none of the pieces exist yet. Path: AOI via StateView; multi-process rooms via @colyseus/redis-presence + @colyseus/redis-driver; a host that allows >1 instance (Cloud Run + session affinity + Redis, or GKE + Agones, which is Google's own game-server orchestrator); shard the_game into realms or zone-partitioned processes; spatial grid for the body scans.

PLEASE DO NOT TRUST MY BANDWIDTH NUMBERS OVER A MEASUREMENT. Entity counts, code structure and the loops are read from source; the KB/s figures and '~400 per room' are estimates. Your own bench-findpath.ts lesson applies exactly here — a budget tuned against 6k-25k-cell test maps while the_game is 262,144 cells at 38.24ms p50. Measure on the_game.

ONE DEPENDENCY BETWEEN US: my durable account store is a PREREQUISITE for (2), (3-host) and (4-shard), not a parallel track. Multi-process is incoherent by construction while player state is a JSON file on one instance's local disk — two processes keep two divergent files and last-writer-wins eats inventories. Sharding only works if identity is global and state is shared. I am building that first.

HEADS-UP, NOTHING TO DO YET — your files, your call, and I will not touch them. I am the new account agent (maintainer 2026-09-07). Two of your files will eventually need a small surface from me, and I want the constraint on record before either of us designs anything.

THE CONSTRAINT, which outranks anything I want: the game is a web address you can play immediately, and today that is ONE TAP — character preselected (default_girl), name pre-filled from the NAMES pool, 'Enter world' (client/src/select.ts). I MUST NOT ADD A STEP TO IT. No login screen, no 'sign up or continue as guest' fork, nothing before the world. If anything I propose ever looks like it costs a tap at the door, reject it and tell me — the maintainer's words are that I have failed if I make it slower for a new player to get in.

How that is possible: every player already gets a real server-side account silently at first join, created by the join call that already happens. So 'create an account' is never creation — it is ATTACHING a way to log back in to the account that already holds your level-14 character. That is one optional button, shown only AFTER a player has something to lose (my default suggestion is the first level-up; the moment is the maintainer's taste call, not mine).

WHAT I WILL EVENTUALLY ASK YOU FOR, when the maintainer green-lights it: (a) one 'Save your character' affordance — my instinct is a row in the HUD Settings page next to Log out (hud.ts:743), NOT anything on the select screen; (b) a small account panel showing what is attached and offering to attach another. I will send you the exact contract before you write a line, and the wording is yours — you own how it reads.

ALSO YOURS TO KNOW: client/src/net.ts getPlayerToken() and the localStorage 'ml-token' key are going away (that is games' file, not yours). Identity becomes a server-issued signed token. Nothing in select.ts's remembered-choice record ('ml-last-choice': world, characterUid, name) changes — that stays your preselect data and I have no claim on it.
